text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Shares closed higher as the equity market gave an initial welcome to the tax plans and economic forecasts in the early part of Chancellor Gordon Brown's budget. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,751.4, up 23.1 points, or 0.49 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares hit record highs as blue chip shares got a strong boost from the firm dollar, always a plus for a market thronged by export-driven firms. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,854.76, up 34.91 points, or 0.91 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,867.53, up 32.69 points, or 0.85 percent.

PARIS - French government threats to tax company profits put paid to a fresh stock market surge after high liquidity, a strong dollar and buoyant overseas markets powered share prices to a new record. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,909.45, down 34.59 points, or 1.17 percent.

ZURICH - Shares ended slightly above Tuesday's closing levels, but operators held back ahead of the outcome of the Federal Reserve's two-day meeting which ends today. The Swiss market index closed at 5,674.3, up 19.5 points, or 0.34 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed well below the highs after reaching new record levels earlier in the day when a large sell order for Telecom Italia was executed just before the market closed. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,494, up 17 points, or 0.13 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares sprinted ahead to close at a new record and dealers foresaw more rises if the Federal Reserve policy makers leave U.S. interst rates unchanged after tonight's meeting. The AEX index closed at 879.02, up 7.71 points, or 0.88 percent.
TOKYO - Stocks closed slightly higher after bouncing back from a morning slump. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,196.42, up 20.90 points, or 0.10 percent.
HONG KONG - The stock market was closed again today as the country celebrates its return to Chinese rule. The market reopens tomorrow.

SYDNEY - The share market streaked to a record close as enthusiastic investors bid the blue chips higher in a broad-based rally. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,745.9, up 24.7 points, or 0.91 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares, unfased by a lower-than-expected reserves figure, climbed to their fifth consecutive record high fuelled by gains in heavyweight stock Richemont. The All-share index closed at 7,416.7, down 3.4 points, or 0.05 percent. The All Gold index closed at 964.7, down 3.9 points, or 0.27 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,832.5, up 23.8 points, or 0.40 percent.
